subject: Geography
description: Important Himalayan + other Indian mountain passes

questions.stem: KHYBER PASS (historical entry route into India) lies in:

options.option_text: Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Hindu Kush)
Sikkim-China border (Nathu La nearby)
Kashmir-Tibet border (Zoji La)
Arunachal-China border (eastern)

questions.explanation: KHYBER PASS — through HINDU KUSH mountains, on Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province). Length 53 km; elevation ~1070 m. HISTORIC INVASION ROUTE into India for ALL major invaders: Aryans, Persians, Greeks (Alexander), Mauryans (other way), Huns, Kushans, Mongols (briefly), Mahmud of Ghazni, Muhammad Ghori, Babur (1526). Connected SILK ROUTE; today connects Peshawar (Pak) to Kabul (Afg). NOW within Pakistan post-1947 (Durand Line). Other historical Indian PASSES: BOLAN PASS (Pak-Afg, alt route through Balochistan); HINDU KUSH passes (Khyber, Khojak). Within MODERN INDIA: NATHU LA (Sikkim-Tibet), ROHTANG (HP), ZOJI LA (J&K-Ladakh), SHIPKI LA, KARAKORAM PASS. India-China BORDER passes used in historical trade.
questions.subject: Geography

options.option_text: Srinagar (Kashmir) to Leh (Ladakh)
Manali to Spiti valley (HP)
Sikkim to Tibet (China) alone
Arunachal to Bhutan (option here)

questions.explanation: ZOJI LA — strategic pass; connects KASHMIR VALLEY (Srinagar) to LADAKH (Kargil + Leh). Elevation ~3528 m. ON NH-1 (national highway). HEAVY SNOW in winter (Nov-May closes); cleared by BRO (Border Roads Org). ZOJI LA TUNNEL (under construction; ~14 km, will be longest road tunnel in Asia at 3000 m altitude) — will keep this strategic route open year-round (vital for army supply to Ladakh + Siachen). 1948 OPERATION ZOJI LA: Indian army recaptured pass from Pakistan in Indo-Pak war (used TANKS at high altitude — first ever). OTHER LADAKH ACCESS: MANALI-LEH highway (via Rohtang + Tang Lang La + Baralacha — many high passes); also via SHYOK + KARAKORAM passes (military). NEW ATAL TUNNEL (2020) under Rohtang — keeps Manali-Leh route accessible longer.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: NATHU LA pass on Sikkim-China border was reopened for trade in:

options.option_text: 2006 (after 44 years closed)
1990 (Cold War end era)
1947 (Independence year)
2020 (recent reopening)

questions.explanation: NATHU LA — pass between SIKKIM (India) + Tibet (China); altitude ~4310 m. CLOSED in 1962 after Sino-Indian war. REOPENED for limited trade in 2006 (after 44 years!). On historic SILK ROUTE branch. Strategic significance: closest land route from India to Lhasa (Tibet); important during 1962 + 1965 wars; 2017 DOKLAM standoff nearby. Nearby: JELEPLA (also pass), GURUDONGMAR LAKE. Other India-China passes (closed for civilian use, often LAC tensions): SHIPKI LA (HP-Tibet), LIPULEKH (Uttarakhand-Tibet), MANA + NITI passes (Uttarakhand). KAILASH-MANSAROVAR YATRA — Indian Hindus go to Mt Kailash via Lipulekh pass (Uttarakhand) or Nathu La. INDIA-CHINA border = LINE OF ACTUAL CONTROL (LAC), 3488 km long, undefined formally.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: BOMDILA + SE LA passes are in which state?

options.option_text: Arunachal Pradesh (NE India)
Sikkim (Nathu La area)
J&K (Zoji La area) alone
Himachal (Rohtang area)

questions.explanation: BOMDILA + SE LA — passes in ARUNACHAL PRADESH; on route from Tezpur (Assam) to TAWANG via West Kameng + Tawang districts. SE LA at 4170 m on Arunachal Pradesh-Tibet border. Strategic — 1962 war battles fought here (CHINA reached Bomdila + Tezpur briefly before withdrawing). SE LA TUNNEL (inaugurated 2024, by Modi): world's longest bi-lane road tunnel above 13,000 ft (~13 km long); year-round access to Tawang for army (vital, given proximity to LAC + 'Arunachal' is claimed by China as 'South Tibet'). Tawang Monastery (Buddhist, 17th century, second-largest in Asia after Lhasa's Potala) — Dalai Lama 6th was born nearby. Recent geopolitical heat: Tawang clash December 2022 (LAC scuffle).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: ROHTANG PASS (now bypassed by Atal Tunnel) connects:

options.option_text: Manali (Kullu) to Lahaul-Spiti valleys (HP)
Srinagar to Jammu (south of Kashmir)
Sikkim to Bhutan (south of Sikkim)
Tamil Nadu to Kerala (Western Ghats)

questions.explanation: ROHTANG PASS — Himachal Pradesh; ~3978 m. Connects Kullu (Manali) to LAHAUL valley + then Spiti, Ladakh. ROHTANG = 'pile of corpses' (Tibetan) — many travellers died crossing in storms historically. Closed Nov-May (snow). ATAL TUNNEL (inaugurated 2020, named after Vajpayee): 9.02 km — bypasses Rohtang, keeps Manali-Lahaul route open year-round. World's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft. Reduced 4-5 hour Manali-Keylong drive to ~10 min via tunnel. Strategic for LADAKH access from Manali side. ROHTANG itself still scenic destination (open in summer; tourism). PARALLEL passes in HP: BARALACHA LA (4890 m, Manali-Leh route), TANGLANG LA (5328 m), KUNZUM LA (Spiti).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: PALGHAT GAP (or Palakkad Gap) is in:

options.option_text: Western Ghats — between Kerala + Tamil Nadu
Himalayas — between Himachal + Punjab
Eastern Ghats — between Andhra + Odisha
Aravalis — between Rajasthan + Gujarat

questions.explanation: PALGHAT GAP / PALAKKAD GAP — major BREAK in Western Ghats; ~40 km wide, between NILGIRI HILLS (north) + ANNAMALAI HILLS (south). Connects Kerala (Palakkad town) + Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore). KEY CORRIDOR for: railway (Tipu Sultan-era; Madras-Cochin RAIL); road (NH 544); MONSOON winds (allows SW monsoon to penetrate Tamil Nadu — explains some TN rainfall). LOCATION strategically + culturally important. OTHER PENINSULAR GAPS in Western Ghats: GOA GAP, BHOR GHAT (near Mumbai-Pune), Thal Ghat. EASTERN GHATS — fragmented, many gaps; rivers cut through (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna delta lowlands).

questions.stem: KARAKORAM PASS (highest pass on India's old SILK ROUTE) is at altitude:

options.option_text: About 5540 m / 18,176 ft
About 3500 m / 11,500 ft (Zoji La)
About 4000 m / 13,000 ft (Nathu La)
About 8000 m / 26,000 ft (Mt Everest)

questions.explanation: KARAKORAM PASS — 5540 m, between LADAKH (India) + Xinjiang (China). One of HIGHEST motorable passes — though motorable now in summer with caution; historically only by yak / mule. Once part of SILK ROUTE branch via Yarkand-Leh. Closed since 1949 (China occupation of Tibet/Xinjiang). India SUSPENDED traffic. KHARDUNG LA (Ladakh, 5359 m) — once claimed 'world's highest motorable road' (claim disputed). UMLING LA (recent, 5883 m, also Ladakh) — currently world's HIGHEST motorable road, opened 2017 by BRO. India is MOUNTAINOUS — many high-altitude road records. CHALLENGES: oxygen ~50% of sea level; vehicles labour; engines need carburettor adjustment.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Lipu Lekh Pass, a key border crossing on the India-China frontier used for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, lies in which Indian state or UT?

options.option_text: Himachal Pradesh, in the Kinnaur district near the Sutlej gorge
Uttarakhand, in the Pithoragarh district of the Kumaon Himalaya
Sikkim, near the Chumbi Valley on the eastern Himalayan front
Ladakh (UT), in the Karakoram range close to the Shyok River

questions.explanation: Lipu Lekh Pass (5,334 m) is in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district (Kumaon Himalaya) and is the traditional route for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. It is also at the centre of the Kalapani territorial dispute between India and Nepal. Option A is wrong — Kinnaur/HP's border crossing with Tibet is Shipki La. Option C is wrong — Sikkim's passes (Nathu La, Jelep La) open into the Chumbi Valley, a different area entirely.

questions.stem: Shipki La pass on the Himachal Pradesh–Tibet border is situated in the valley of which river that enters India through this very pass?

options.option_text: Beas River, draining the Kullu Valley before entering the Punjab plains
Sutlej River, one of the five rivers of Punjab, entering India via Shipki La
Chenab River, originating near Bara Lacha La in the Lahaul district
Spiti River, a cold-desert tributary of the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: The Sutlej River (called Langchen Khamab in Tibet) enters India through Shipki La in Kinnaur district, HP. Option D (Spiti) is the most tempting distractor — the Spiti also drains into the Sutlej, but it does not cross Shipki La. Option C (Chenab) is wrong; the Chenab's headwaters (Chandra and Bhaga) originate near Bara Lacha La, a completely different pass further northwest.

questions.stem: Jelep La pass, the preferred British-era trade and diplomatic route between Sikkim and Lhasa, connects to which specific Tibetan valley on its northern side?

options.option_text: Yarlung Tsangpo Valley, the Tibetan upper course of the Brahmaputra River
Chumbi Valley, a strategic Tibetan salient flanked by Sikkim and Bhutan
Qinghai Plateau, the inland high-altitude tableland of central Tibet
Aksai Chin, the disputed high-altitude plateau in the western Tibet region

questions.explanation: Jelep La (4,267 m) was the main British trade and postal route and opens northward into the Chumbi Valley — a narrow Tibetan tongue projecting south between Sikkim and Bhutan. This valley's dagger-like shape pointing at the Siliguri Corridor makes it among the most strategically watched pieces of terrain in the eastern Himalayas. Nathu La (already asked) also accesses the same Chumbi Valley but at a different point. Options A and C are inner-Tibet features far north of Jelep La's immediate exit.

questions.stem: Pin Parvati Pass (5,319 m), a high-altitude trekking route in Himachal Pradesh, connects the lush Parvati Valley in Kullu district to which arid cold-desert valley?

options.option_text: Lahaul Valley, which is also accessible via Rohtang and Bara Lacha La passes
Pin Valley in Spiti district, a cold-desert tributary of the Spiti River
Baspa Valley in Kinnaur district, known for apple orchards and Chitkul village
Sangla Valley in Kinnaur, following the Baspa River towards the Tibetan border

questions.explanation: Pin Parvati Pass links the green Parvati Valley (Kullu) with Pin Valley (Spiti district), famous for its Buddhist monasteries and cold-desert terrain — a rare crossing of the Great Himalayan Range entirely within HP. The dramatic biome contrast makes this pass distinctive. Option A (Lahaul) is wrong — Lahaul is reached via Rohtang Pass or Hampta Pass, not Pin Parvati. Options C and D (Kinnaur valleys) are on the opposite, southeastern side of the range.

questions.stem: Pangsau Pass in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district, nicknamed the 'Pass of No Return', connects India to which country, and why did it earn that grim name?

options.option_text: China (Yunnan Province); Indian soldiers crossed it in retreat during the 1962 India-China War
Myanmar (Sagaing Region); Allied troops fleeing the Japanese advance in World War II perished crossing it
Bhutan (Trashigang district); British colonial forces retreated through it during the 1942 Burma campaign
Bangladesh (Sylhet division); refugees crossed it fleeing violence during the 1971 Liberation War

questions.explanation: Pangsau Pass (~1,000 m) on the India-Myanmar border (Patkai Hills) earned the epithet 'Pass of No Return' because thousands of British-Indian soldiers and civilians died crossing it while retreating from Japanese forces in Burma in 1942. The Stilwell Road (Ledo Road) built by Allied forces also passes through here. Option A is a planted distractor — the 1962 War was with China, and China-border passes are in very different terrain. Option C is a subtle trap: Bhutan is wrong — the border is India-Myanmar.

questions.stem: The Sela Tunnel, inaugurated in March 2024 to ensure all-weather road access to Tawang district, was built below which pass that fell to Chinese forces within days during the 1962 India-China War?

options.option_text: Bum La Pass (~4,700 m), located on the Line of Actual Control near Tawang town itself
Sela Pass (~4,170 m), a snow-bound choke point that cut off Tawang for months each year
Bomdila Pass (~2,700 m), the administrative district headquarters of West Kameng district
Dirang Pass (~1,500 m), a lower valley crossing on the road before ascending towards Sela

questions.explanation: Sela Pass (4,170 m) in Arunachal Pradesh was the critical choke point on the Bomdila–Tawang road. Its loss in November 1962 exposed Tawang. Being snow-bound for months also severed civilian and military supply lines each winter. The Sela Tunnel (a twin-tube project: 980 m + 1,555 m tubes) was inaugurated by PM Modi on 9 March 2024. Option A (Bum La) is wrong — Bum La is further north on the LAC, not on the main supply highway; it is used only for a flag-meeting post. Option C (Bomdila) is the town below the pass, not the pass that the tunnel bypasses.

questions.stem: Khardung La pass in Ladakh is the primary land supply artery for Indian Army logistics to the Siachen Glacier. Beyond this military role, the pass opens road access to which valley north of Leh?

options.option_text: Zanskar Valley, a remote high-altitude valley to the south of Leh in Ladakh
Nubra Valley, the confluence of the Shyok and Nubra rivers lying north of Leh
Markha Valley, a trekking route running parallel to the Indus east of Leh town
Pangong basin, the area around the high-altitude tectonic lake on the India-China LAC

questions.explanation: Khardung La (5,359 m) is the gateway from Leh northward to Nubra Valley (Shyok–Nubra confluence). From Nubra, military supply columns continue to Siachen Glacier base areas — making this route of acute strategic importance. Option A (Zanskar) is wrong — Zanskar lies south of Leh and is accessed via Pensi La or the Zanskar River route, not Khardung La. Option D (Pangong) is reached via Chang La, a separate pass to the east of Leh. Students often confuse Chang La and Khardung La.
